reason:
The load-bearing half of this finding is a measurement artifact of the reviewer's own test, and the fix regresses the thing the plan is actually made of.

1. The bad break the finding is built on cannot occur. fixture.js already welds the joint the fix proposes to weld: `var NB = " "` and `longYear = weekday + " " + day + NB + month + NB + year`, with a comment stating the intent verbatim - "the ceremonial date can break after the weekday but never between the 3 and the October... only this one joint is welded". Driving the master and rendering through the real formatter at 1024/1152/1440, every date that wraps wraps in exactly one place: "Saturday" (116px) / "12 September 2026" (257px); "Wednesday" (152) / "23 September 2026" (263). I could only reproduce the reported "Saturday 12" / "September 2026" (150 / 222) by writing a plain-ASCII-space string into .b-when, i.e. by bypassing the formatter - which is what the finding did when it "typed dates into it". The second clause of the proposed fix is therefore already shipped, and the first clause's entire emotional argument rests on a break the artifact does not produce.

2. The gate citation is wrong. "no date breaks in half" asserts on .b-behindDate in the record's past lane at 390px, not on .b-when. It does not pass "because that string was the one chosen"; it never looks at the ceremonial date.

3. The width numbers are right and irrelevant. Confirmed: .b-when box is 344px at all three widths, fixture date inks 330px (14px slack), other dates go 39px -> 78px. But two lines is a designed, balanced (text-wrap: balance), left-ragged setting under the 79 figure - "Saturday" over "12 September 2026" - in a sticky column whose height is 377px against a 1727px measure. It costs nothing and reads as a wedding invitation reads. That is a decision, not a defect.

4. The fix makes it worse where it matters. The finding argues from 1440, where the measure column is 668px. The proposed rule starts at 1024, where that column is 432px, not 668px. Applying `grid-template-columns: 420px minmax(0,1fr)` I measured the measure column drop 432 -> 356 at 1024, and two of the seven moment titles wrap to two lines (title height 29 -> 58, row height 79 -> 108). It buys one line back on the horizon by spending two lines on the moments - the actual plan - at precisely the laptop band round 7 just paid to bring into the two-column composition. Trading a graceful, deliberate break on a display date for wrapped content titles is the wrong side of that trade.

5. On the round-7 constraint: 420 happens not to break "today is one mark at every width" (the rule measures 420 uniformly at 701/1152/1279/1280/1440, since the 701 track is 509px wide), so the finding survives that specific hurdle - but it does not survive point 1 or point 4.

Refuted: factually wrong about how the string breaks, half already handled, and the fix regresses row titles at 1024.
